findings.where: First-screen nav: 'Profile', 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog', at both widths
findings.fault: The three nav links go to one place, the article specimen (#article). If you click 'Profile' to see who Mark is, you land on a 2024 blog post about PPP law. Each label promises a different place, and none of them takes you to a different one.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer checking Mark's background before writing. 'Profile' is where they would look for his experience, and they get an opinion piece instead. The founder would object too, since they try the first screen first.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row under the article ('Streamlining the PPP Process … Lecture · 23 April 2026' with a download arrow and 'PDF')
findings.fault: The download arrow and the blue 'PDF' say that clicking gets you a file. In fact the whole row is one link back to #article on this page, so no PDF opens. The lecture title, which is most of what you can click, is plain grey serif, so only the small 'PDF' looks clickable.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the lecture slides. They click 'PDF' and nothing downloads, and they don't think to click the title. The research calls the PDF list 'the product', so this is the part that has to work.

findings.where: Article specimen, the numbers of the three-item list (blue 1., 2., 3.)
findings.fault: The list numbers use the link blue, but you can't click them. The page's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', and here the link colour goes on plain text, so blue stops meaning 'link'.
findings.who_objects: A reader who taps a blue number expecting it to jump somewhere. Angélique would object too: she maintains the site from the stated rule, and the specimen breaks it.

findings.where: First-screen nav lockup: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark, at both widths
findings.fault: Mark's name comes first, but it is set small and light. The bold white arches and capital 'MMM INFRA' next to it are bigger and brighter. When you squint, the firm's mark wins over the man's name.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test asks for 'his name leads, with the logo beside it'. The weight here does the opposite of the order.

findings.where: First-screen logo (mark and 'MMM INFRA' reversed to warm white on slate)
findings.fault: The logo is shown in an all-white version that Mark doesn't hold. The house rule says a version like this is made only once the client agrees, and nothing on the tile says it is a proposed version waiting for his yes.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo colours are fixed until he opens them. The founder would also object to showing an unapproved logo version as if it were settled.

findings.where: Hero photograph's keyed edge (around the hair and at the lower right) and the 'Graded for the site' image in the Texture section
findings.fault: Swapping the purple backdrop for slate leaves a soft pale halo around his head and a cut wedge across the lectern. The photo reads as a cut-out pasted onto navy, not a man speaking in real light. This is the candidate's own grading step, not the stand-in photo.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asks for 'refined, never childish' and real people in real light. A visitor from a development bank who spots the edge may take it as amateur photo editing, on the one screen meant to win their trust.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row placed straight after the article body
findings.fault: A different lecture from 2026 sits under the 2024 blog post with no heading such as 'Talks' or 'Related'. Its hairlines frame it as part of the article, so it reads as this post's own attachment.
findings.who_objects: A reader who downloads it expecting this article as a PDF and gets a different talk.

findings.where: First-screen nav, 'Articles and talks' next to 'Blog'
findings.fault: Blog posts are also articles, so the two labels overlap, and a visitor can't tell which one holds a given piece of Mark's writing.
findings.who_objects: A returning reader looking for one of Mark's pieces, who has to try both. Angélique would also have to decide where every new post belongs.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row's title and 'Lecture · date' line; the byline under the article title
findings.fault: The lecture row's text starts about 4 px to the right of the article column's left edge, so it sits slightly out of line with everything above it. The byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024' is pressed right up against the title, much tighter than every other gap in the article.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the article specimen as proof of the type rhythm the brief asks for. A small offset and one cramped gap undercut a section whose stated point is that everything sits on one rhythm.
